INVH.thesis_one_line: Large landlord of about 85,500 rented family houses, buying back stock and selling homes above its share-price value, but fairly priced for modest rent growth.
kill_criteria: Net debt / TTM adjusted EBITDAre above 6.0x (8-K Ex. 99.1 Schedule 2(b); 5.4x at 30 Jun 2026).
Same Store NOI growth at or below 0.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q1-26 was -0.3%, Q2-26 +1.5%).
Same Store average occupancy below 95.5% in any quarter (Q4-25 low was 95.9%).
Full-year Core FFO per share guidance midpoint cut below $1.90 (current $1.95).
Enacted federal or state law that forces divestiture or caps rents on existing wholly owned homes (the ROAD Act has no divestiture requirement).
key_adverse_facts: Same-store NOI growth fell from +4.7% (Q4-24) to -0.3% (Q1-26); Q2-26 +1.5%; 2026 guide +0.4% to +1.9%
ROAD to Housing Act (law 11 Jul 2026) bars 350+-home investors from buying existing homes from 7 Jan 2027; build-to-rent exempt; 10-Q says institutional buyers are deferring BTR/fee-build purchases
Refinancing: new 4.950% notes vs 3.9% book average; $988M 2027 secured debt (now partly prepaid)
Buybacks funded by asset sales and leverage, not free cash flow; FY25 Core FFO $1.91 finished one cent below the raised $1.92 midpoint
data_conflicts: V1 'excessive' verdict and 36x NTM P/E use GAAP EPS/EBIT with D&A set to zero; on AFFO the multiple is 16.1x (Core FFO 13.7x)
d4/d3 FCF yield 7.4-7.6% deducts about $4M capex; INVH spends about $165M a year recurring capex (AFFO deduction)
INVH.confidence_in_thesis: medium: primary filings fully opened; NAV and ROAD Act effects not quantified from filings

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1 excessive rests on GAAP EPS/EBIT reverse DCF with D&A=0 (40% implied growth), inapplicable to a REIT; on AFFO the implied growth is 4.4%/yr vs my 3.0% base, so fair-to-slightly-rich, not excessive.

INVH.scenario_basis: Start 2026 AFFO/share $1.65 (guidance midpoint), dividend $1.20; bear AFFO -1%/yr exit 12.5x; base +3%/yr exit 15.5x, dividend +3%; bull +6%/yr exit 18x; price $26.62.

UNP.thesis_one_line: Western US freight railroad with strong pricing and record results, buying Norfolk Southern; good business, but the price already assumes high-single-digit earnings growth.
kill_criteria: Reported operating ratio at or above 61.5% for two consecutive quarters (Q2-26 59.7%; 8-K Ex. 99.1 income statement).
Freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge growth below 1% y/y for two consecutive quarters (Q2-26 +4%).
Adjusted debt / adjusted EBITDA above 3.0x on a standalone basis (10-Q MD&A table; 2.5x at 30 Jun 2026), or management-stated pro forma leverage above 3.5x at closing.
STB denies the application, or UPC/NSC terminate (the $2.5B fee applies in certain cases).
Guidance cut: 2026 reported EPS growth outlook reduced below "mid-single digit" (currently "high-single digit").
key_adverse_facts: Q2-26 reported operating ratio worsened 70 bp y/y to 59.7% on fuel; effective tax rate 22.0% vs 18.9%
H1-26 cash taxes $236M vs $785M: about $550M of OCF improvement is timing
NSC deal: about 225M new shares (+38%), about $20B cash consideration, $2.5B termination fee in certain cases; STB review, close guided 2027
Buybacks paused ($26M H1-26 vs $2,679M H1-25); debt fair value $24.7B vs carrying $30.3B
data_conflicts: Triage cited 29% margin and 40% ROE; filings show Q2-26 operating margin 40.3% and b1 ROE 35.5%
V1 reverse DCF suppressed (D&A missing); own EPS-based reverse DCF gives 7.7%/yr
d4 FCF yield 2.9% (after dividends) vs TTM OCF less capex 4.0%
UNP.confidence_in_thesis: medium: standalone numbers solid; merger terms and timeline from 10-Q but synergy and pro forma leverage not verified

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Agree with V1 demanding: implied 10-year EPS growth 7.7% vs my 6.5% base; my base 3y return 5.0% vs V1 2.9% differs only through dividends and exit multiple. [DV41 2026-10-08: programme basis (Ke 9.22%, FCF after SBC) implies 8.7-9.9%/yr: above, wider than stated.]

UNP.scenario_basis: Start 2026E GAAP EPS $13.06 (consensus FY0), dividend $5.60 growing 4%; bear EPS -2%/yr exit 16x; base +6.5%/yr exit 19x; bull +10%/yr exit 21x; price $273.79; merger excluded.

COO.thesis_one_line: Maker of contact lenses and fertility products, cheap after two guidance cuts and a failed sale process, with heavy buybacks but stalled lens growth.
kill_criteria: CooperVision organic revenue growth below -1% in fiscal Q1-27 (quarter ending 31 Jan 2027), after the Q4-26 guide of "-2% to 0%" (8-K Ex. 99.1 segment table).
FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance midpoint below $4.40, or FY26 actual non-GAAP EPS below $4.51 (bottom of the Q3-26 range).
Free cash flow (OCF less capex) for fiscal 2027 below $600M on the company's definition, or cumulative FY26-28 objective of "exceeding $2.2 billion" withdrawn.
Total debt to non-GAAP EBITDA above 2.5x (10-Q Note 4 debt $2,544.2M today; about 1.8x derived), or covenant waiver.
Any new litigation charge above $100M (recall or HMRC: the HMRC range is £0 to £71.7M plus interest).
key_adverse_facts: FY26 guidance cut twice: revenue midpoint $4.326B -> $4.303B -> $4.2405B; EPS midpoint $4.62 -> $4.53 (new top below old bottom)
CooperVision organic 0% in Q3-26, guided -2% to 0% for Q4; US channel inventory reduction
Fertility recall claims: $272.0M net charge in nine months; $306.8M paid Aug 2026 (about $263M net cash)
HMRC Sauflon payroll-tax dispute: FTT sided largely with HMRC; exposure GBP 0 to 71.7M plus interest, no liability recorded
Board rejected offers for CooperSurgical; non-hormonal IUD entrant named as a valuation factor
data_conflicts: Triage said revenue growth +0.6% flatlined (latest quarter only); nine-month growth is +4.8%
GAAP EPS $2.24 in Q3-26 includes a $307.2M discrete UK tax benefit; non-GAAP $1.15
TTM FCF $678M includes $111M working-capital inflow and excludes the August settlement cash
COO.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low: filings opened, but guidance credibility is falling and the December date is an estimate

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. My reverse DCF on normalized free cash flow ($600M) at a 10% cost of equity implies 5.6%/yr vs a 6% base; base return 6.8%/yr is below the 10% required return, hence WATCH. [DV10 2026-10-09: restated. Normalized FCF of $600M added back SBC (~$70M); with SBC as a cost (~$530M) implied growth is 7.3%/yr vs the 6% base, i.e. above. WATCH unchanged.]

COO.scenario_basis: Start FY26 non-GAAP EPS $4.53 (guide midpoint), no dividend; bear EPS -1%/yr exit 10x; base +6%/yr (organic 2-3% plus buyback shrink) exit 12.5x; bull +10%/yr exit 15x; price $55.38.
